summary: Discovery focused on log retention, legal-hold processes, and whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private best fits Northpoint Savings' regulatory needs. Key constraints: strict 7-year retention for transactional logs, legal hold overrides, SOC2+HIPAA applicability in parts of product, and tight RBAC/KMS requirements.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-30 16:00 UTC — Duration 57m — Attendees: Janelle Park (Redwood AE), Marco Rossi (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood Solutions); Martin Hale (CISO, Northpoint), Leah Ortiz (Head of Cloud Eng), Samir Patel (Compliance), Dana Nguyen (Legal)

[00:00] Janelle: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros and we'll jump into the legal/retention constraints you sent.
[00:12] Martin: Hi, Martin here. I'll be driving security and compliance reqs. We've got a fairly prescriptive retention schedule — core transactional logs seven years, with some subsets ten years because of state regs.
[00:25] Leah: And on the infra side, we run in multi-region cloud but data residency is a hard requirement for EU accounts. We need region-locking for EU customers.
[00:36] Marco: Thanks — to confirm, when you say transactional logs, is that application-level request logs, full request+response, or redacted token counts?
[00:46] Samir: Good question. For the finance product, legal wants full request metadata and request IDs retained. The actual payloads — should be redacted unless they're required for dispute resolution. We also have to preserve copies for e-discovery if legal hold is issued.
[01:02] Dana: Right, legal-hold is a big one. If there's a subpoena or regulatory exam we need to freeze and export a consistent set of artifacts — traces, audit logs, request IDs, the prompts used plus the model output in some cases.
[01:15] Priya: One thing to flag — Redwood's hosted API stores logs for X days by default, but we support Dedicated and Private where you control retention. Marco, want to go over options quickly?
[01:27] Marco: Sure. There are three patterns: hosted default (short retention, easier onboarding), dedicated reserved capacity (you can configure retention and have isolated GPU pools), and private (VPC/on-prem, control plane separated, you manage keys and retention fully). For legal-hold we usually recommend dedicated or private because hosted is harder to guarantee long-term immutability.
[01:46] Leah: When you say "control plane separated" for private, do we still get the console and audit traces? We need immutable audit trails for SOC2.
[01:54] Janelle: Yes — with Private we provide a customer-controlled control plane endpoint, and audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. You can also opt for a read-only external archive for immutability.
[02:06] Martin: How about KMS? Keys must be resident in our region and we need HSM-backed rotation policies.
[02:13] Marco: We support KMS integrations — Cloud KMS, dedicated HSMs and bring-your-own-key. For private deployments keys can remain exclusively in your VPC/HSM; for dedicated we can do customer-managed keys via a hybrid setup.
[02:25] Samir: Another run — do you keep full request/response in logs by default? We want to avoid storing PII in cleartext in logs.
[02:33] Priya: Default is we capture call metadata and minimal request payload for metrics. For hosted customers who opt-in to long retention there's an opt-in box and encryption at rest. We also offer a redaction pipeline to strip PII tokens from transcripts automatically, but there will be edge cases.
[02:48] Dana: Edge cases are the problem. Legal will need the original for investigations sometimes. If we redact and then later need originals, how do we produce them?
[02:57] Marco: Two strategies: 1) Keep originals in a segregated encrypted archive with strict access controls and audit trails; 2) Keep only encrypted blobs where keys can be escrowed for e-discovery. For customers with strict legal-hold, we usually recommend segregated archival in the same region and RBAC gating.
[03:15] Martin: Escrow becomes a governance headache. We prefer customer-held keys and an exportable archive.
[03:21] Janelle: Makes sense. We'll flag that as a requirement.
[03:25] [03:30] Leah: From performance side, what are SLO impacts if we enable long-tail archival or synchronous archive-on-write? We can't degrade p99s for front-line latency.
[03:40] Marco: Archive-on-write is async. The runtime will return generated tokens while a background worker forwards logs to the archive. That keeps p50/p95 low. If you need synchronous, that's a custom trade and will affect latency. We can show numbers in the pilot.
[03:55] Samir: On retention windows — can we set per-route retention? For example, KYC routes get ten years, payments seven years, analytics 90 days.
[04:07] Priya: Yes, per-route retention is supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted can do tagging but not guaranteed long-term immutability.
[04:17] Martin: Also need to understand deletion workflows — when legal hold is not present, but retention lapses, do we have deterministic deletion? And can we prove deletion for auditors?
[04:27] Marco: We provide cryptographic deletion proof — log entries showing deletion commands, tombstone markers, and storage-level zeroization on supported providers. For Private you control the deletion toolchain so auditors can review processes.
[04:41] Dana: Can Redwood provide sample audit language and artifacts? Our auditors will ask for chain of custody.
[04:47] Janelle: Yes, we'll send a SOC2+HIPAA mapping and a sample chain-of-custody playbook.
[04:52] [05:00] Leah: A technical nit — KV cache and prefix caching: if you do caching across customers, we need strict tenant isolation.
[05:07] Marco: KV cache is per-tenant on Dedicated/Private. Hosted has shared pools with strict logical separation but we know auditors sometimes flag that. We can show cache isolation configurations in the design doc.
[05:20] Martin: Multi-region failover: if EU region becomes unavailable, will we failover to US? That could violate residency. We need region-first routing with no cross-border fallback for EU accounts.
[05:33] Priya: You can set routing policy by account. For EU accounts choose "region-lock — no cross-border fallback" or "region-preferred" for less strict.
[05:43] Samir: About logs — do you redact tokens used for billing? We need token-level cost visibility but not raw prompts in infra logs.
[05:52] Marco: We expose token counts, model versions, latencies per request without storing full prompt in metrics logs. If you want prompt-level tracing, that's optional and stored in encrypted archive.
[06:05] Dana: Legal-hold export format? We need document-friendly exports, with verifiable checksums and manifest files.
[06:12] Marco: We'll provide exports as compressed archives (tar.gz) with manifest.json listing SHA256 checksums, request IDs and timestamps. For Private, you can configure the manifest schema to match e-discovery tools.
[06:24] [06:30] Martin: Any regulatory certs? SOC2 is baseline, do you have HIPAA BAAs for hosted?
[06:37] Janelle: Redwood has SOC2 Type II, and we offer HIPAA BAA for eligible customers; for Private deployments we support BAA terms but legal needs to sign separate annex.
[06:50] Martin: And data residency evidence for EU — are logs and backups provably stored in region?
[06:57] Marco: We can provide storage proofs — account-level region tags, immutable archives in region, and operators logs showing no cross-region replication. It is part of our evidence pack.
[07:07] Leah: One more — RBAC/SSO. We require SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained roles mapped to our HR groups.
[07:16] Priya: Supported. In Private/Dedicated you can use your IdP and SCIM for provisioning; hosted supports SSO+SCIM but for fine-grained host-level roles we recommend Dedicated.
[07:27] Dana: If we go Dedicated, what is the timeline to get started and what kind of maintenance windows?
[07:33] Janelle: On a reserved capacity Dedicated contract we can provision in 4–6 weeks typically; Private takes longer depending on network integrations. Maintenance windows are negotiable and tracked in the SLA.
[07:44] Samir: Pricing question — is long retention billed as storage+ingress/egress or a single per-GB per-month?
[07:52] Marco: Storage is billed as GB-month plus an archival access fee for e-discovery exports; we can scope pricing in the follow-up quote.
[07:59] Leah: For the pilot we want a throughput test: 20 concurrent engines for peak payment flows and a legal-hold export exercise. Can Redwood support trace-level capture for that?
[08:10] Marco: Yes — we'll set up a dedicated pilot cluster with tracing enabled and a synthetic legal-hold drill. We'll redact live PII in test vectors but preserve necessary fields to validate workflows.
[08:24] Janelle: Great — let's recap next steps. We'll send the SOC2+HIPAA mapping, proposed Dedicated config and latency/cost estimate, and a one-pager on legal-hold exports. You (Northpoint) will send retention matrix and legal examples.
[08:36] Dana: Expect those docs from legal by Friday.
[08:39] Martin: Also please include references or case studies where Redwood handled similar long-tail retention in finance.
[08:46] Janelle: We'll include two redacted case studies and connect you with an existing customer reference.
[08:50] [08:55] Priya: Quick technical aside — some transcriptions: we sometimes see mislabels in auto transcripts, so the export we send will be cleaned.
[09:02] Leah: Good. Anything else?
[09:05] Samir: Not from compliance.
[09:07] Martin: No. Thanks.
[09:10] Janelle: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the pilot kickoff.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quirks: occasional mis-heard acronyms ("sock two" for SOC2, "S S O" spaced), small filler words, and a couple speaker label swaps early in recording.
